headline: Dhaka traffic: PM orders relocation of three bus terminals to ease congestion
summary: The Prime Minister has reviewed progress on traffic measures and directed the movement of key terminals to reduce city gridlock.
details: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ordered the relocation of three major bus terminals in Dhaka to alleviate the city's chronic traffic congestion.
caption:
Three major bus terminals are moving out of Dhaka to fight traffic gridlock.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ordered the relocation of three major bus terminals in Dhaka to alleviate the city's chronic traffic congestion.

headline_marked: HC seeks report on [[children living in prisons]] with incarcerated mothers
headline: HC seeks report on children living in prisons with incarcerated mothers
summary: The High Court has ordered prison authorities to provide the number and age profile of children staying in jails across the country.
details: The High Court has sought a detailed report from prison authorities regarding the number and age profile of children currently living in prisons with their incarcerated mothers across Bangladesh.
A bench comprising Justice Khizir Ahmed Choudhury and Justice Md Ziaul Haque issued the directive, ordering the inspector general of prisons to submit the report within two months.
The court also issued a rule asking government authorities to explain why steps should not be taken to ensure the safety, welfare, education, and fundamental rights of these children.
The order follows a writ petition filed by Supreme Court lawyer Quamrun Nahar Mahmud Deepa, who highlighted the lack of adequate provisions for children in such environments.
Deputy Attorney General Md Faruk Hossein stated that the safety, education, and development of children living in prisons are not being adequately ensured.
The petitioner sought necessary directives from the High Court to safeguard the fundamental rights of these children who are staying in jails through no fault of their own.
caption:
How many children are living in Bangladesh's prisons? The High Court has demanded a full report on their age and numbers.

The High Court has sought a detailed report from prison authorities regarding the number and age profile of children currently living in prisons with their incarcerated mothers across Bangladesh.

A bench comprising Justice Khizir Ahmed Choudhury and Justice Md Ziaul Haque issued the directive, ordering the inspector general of prisons to submit the report within two months.

The court also issued a rule asking government authorities to explain why steps should not be taken to ensure the safety, welfare, education, and fundamental rights of these children.

The order follows a writ petition filed by Supreme Court lawyer Quamrun Nahar Mahmud Deepa, who highlighted the lack of adequate provisions for children in such environments.

Deputy Attorney General Md Faruk Hossein stated that the safety, education, and development of children living in prisons are not being adequately ensured.

The petitioner sought necessary directives from the High Court to safeguard the fundamental rights of these children who are staying in jails through no fault of their own.

#Bangladesh #HighCourt #HumanRights #ChildWelfare #Justice

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Somoy News
